title: Rigveda 9.16: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.16: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.16 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 674v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.16.1-8 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 674v
translation.original_text:
1pra te̍ so̱tāra̍ o̱ṇyo̱3̱̍ rasa̱m madā̍ya̱ ghṛṣva̍ye | sargo̱ na ta̱kty eta̍śaḥ ||
2kratvā̱ dakṣa̍sya ra̱thya̍m a̱po vasā̍na̱m andha̍sā | go̱ṣām aṇve̍ṣu saścima ||
3ana̍ptam a̱psu du̱ṣṭara̱ṁ soma̍m pa̱vitra̱ ā sṛ̍ja | pu̱nī̱hīndrā̍ya̱ pāta̍ve ||
4pra pu̍nā̱nasya̱ ceta̍sā̱ soma̍ḥ pa̱vitre̍ arṣati | kratvā̍ sa̱dhastha̱m āsa̍dat ||
5pra tvā̱ namo̍bhi̱r inda̍va̱ indra̱ somā̍ asṛkṣata | ma̱he bharā̍ya kā̱riṇa̍ḥ ||
6pu̱nā̱no rū̱pe a̱vyaye̱ viśvā̱ arṣa̍nn a̱bhi śriya̍ḥ | śūro̱ na goṣu̍ tiṣṭhati ||
7di̱vo na sānu̍ pi̱pyuṣī̱ dhārā̍ su̱tasya̍ ve̱dhasa̍ḥ | vṛthā̍ pa̱vitre̍ arṣati ||
8tvaṁ so̍ma vipa̱ścita̱ṁ tanā̍ punā̱na ā̱yuṣu̍ | avyo̱ vāra̱ṁ vi dhā̍vasi ||
translation.text:
1THE pressers from the Soma-press send forth thy juice for rapturous joy The speckled sap runs like a flood.
2With strength we follow through the sieve him who brings might and wins the kine, Enrobed in water with his juice.
3Pour on the sieve the Soma, ne'er subdued in waters, waterless, And make it pure for Indra's drink.
4Moved by the purifier's thought, the Soma flows into the sieve: By wisdom it hath gained its home.
5With humble homage, Indra, have the Soma-drops flowed forth to thee, Contending for the glorious prize.
6Purified in his fleecy garb, attaining every beauty, he Stands, hero-like, amid the kine.
7Swelling, as 'twere, to heights of heaven, the stream of the creative juice Falls lightly on the cleansing sieve.
8Thus, Soma, purifying himwho knoweth song mid living men, Thou wanderest through the cloth of wool.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 674v (numbered 96v by the scribe) (OPenn image 675, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.15.8 ‹iti tyam daśa kṣipaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 675r (numbered 97r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.17.1 ‹āśavaḥ›. Verses 9.16.1-8 end on this page.
